confidence.note: Juicero's own pack yield, pack COGS and retention were not public before 2016-03-01; a teardown or pack cost sheet would raise it.

gross_margin.note: Est. 28% per $6.50 pack after produce, pouch and cold-chain delivery; bottled juice targets ~60%. R5: costs_eat_margin.

ltv_cac.note: Est. LTV $390 vs CAC $200 (CPC / 0.75% conversion): LTV:CAC 1.95, before any hardware subsidy.

pricing_power.note: Anchor is falling: Suja cut 16oz to $7.99 and launched $3.99; Costco sells it at $0.17/oz.

build_effort.note: Custom high-force press plus a produce-pack plant: over 6 months; still unlaunched after raising since 2013.

skills_match.note: Hardware team in place; food safety, fresh-produce sourcing and cold chain are new skills.

capital_needed.note: About $20M raised and ~$120M being raised: fits, but hardware plus a food plant burns capital fast.

time_to_mvp.note: Over 2 years from seed (2013) with no product on sale by early 2016.

sales_cycle.note: $699 considered consumer purchase: days to weeks, not impulse.

channel_readiness.note: Direct online plus tech press exists; CAC for a $699 device unproven (est. $100-$300).

search_demand.note: Juice bars a $2.2B US industry riding the cold-pressed craze; active cleanse culture.

trend.note: Super-premium cold-pressed juice +130.5% YoY (IRI, 52 weeks to 2015-03).

willingness_to_pay.note: Buyers pay up to $10 a 16oz bottle, but leaders are cutting prices to widen the market.

free_alternatives.note: No free equivalent, but $70-$400 juicers and $3.99-$8 bottles do much of the job.

competitor_density.note: Suja ($45M revenue, Coca-Cola $90M stake), Evolution Fresh, Jamba, Pressed Juicery. R5: strong_competitor.

differentiation.note: Only connected juicer found: fresh-pressed at home with no cleanup is a real, specific difference.

legal_regulatory.note: Raw cut-produce plant under new FSMA rules (2015); unpasteurized juice E. coli outbreaks in 2015.

platform_dependency.note: Owns its channel, but each pack needs a server check: Wink hubs bricked by one expired certificate.

market_risk.note: Cold-pressed may be a fad: pioneer chain Organic Avenue shut all 10 stores in 2015-10.

skills.note: Funded hardware team; no pre-2016 evidence of food-manufacturing track record.

assets.note: Kleiner Perkins and Campbell's backing: capital and food-industry network.

interest.note: Founder motivation not documented in pre-2016 sources: scored neutral.

som.reasoning: 5,000 households x ($699 press + 260 packs x $6.50 = $1,690) = $11.9M, ~1.4% of the $844.6M cold-pressed SAM

competitors_found.reasoning: Counted: Suja, Evolution Fresh, BluePrint, Jamba, Pressed Juicery, Juice Press, Costco/retail bottles, Omega, Hurom, Hamilton Beach juicers

price.reasoning: Midpoint of the brief's $5-$8 pack price; no pre-2016 source discloses Juicero pricing

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: 8oz pack: ~0.8 lb organic produce at ~$2/lb = $1.75 + pouch and labor $0.75 + cold-chain box ~$11.50 / ~6 packs = $2.00 + spoilage $0.20 = $4.70

gross_margin_pct.reasoning: (6.50 - 4.70) / 6.50 = 27.7%, packs only; press assumed sold near cost

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Assumption: no pre-2016 retention benchmark for perishable subscriptions found; 10%/month used

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: US e-commerce averages 3.06% (Monetate 2015); a $699 considered purchase assumed at 0.5-1%, midpoint 0.75%

cac.reasoning: Blended CPC: Facebook $0.31-$0.85, Google $2.32; / 0.5-1% conversion = $31-$464; midpoint ~$200

ltv.reasoning: 5 packs/week x 4.33 = 21.65 packs x $6.50 = $140.7/month x 27.7% margin x 10 months = $390

payback_months.reasoning: CAC $200 / $39 monthly gross profit per subscriber = 5.1 months

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Assumption: ~50 staff x ~$15k loaded cost + pack facility and leases ~ $1M/month

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: $1,000,000 fixed / $39 gross profit per subscriber per month = 25,641 active subscribers

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: Not on sale as of 2016-03-01 after raising since 2013; at least one quarter to launch and deliver (assumption)

launch_reason: Founder and investors are in the Bay Area, where premium cold-pressed buyers concentrate.
cheapest_test: 7-day fake-door in the Bay Area: $699 press pre-order with $50 refundable deposit plus hand-delivered pack trial to 20 households
kill_criteria: Fewer than 300 paid $50 deposits on the Bay Area landing page by day 7 -> stop
Measured cold-chain cost per weekly box above $10 in the day 5 test delivery -> stop
Fewer than 3 packs per week per tester household in the day 1-7 trial -> stop

rescue.change: Drop the press: sell the same organic juice as HPP bottles through grocery retail
rescue.why: Fixes costs_eat_margin (bottled juice ~60% margin) and build_effort; still faces strong_competitor Suja
rescue.requires: Beverage distribution contacts and a brand that beats Suja on shelf

rescue.change: Sell the press to offices, gyms and cafes with daily pack volume
rescue.why: Fixes contribution_margin: one cold-chain drop serves 30+ packs a day instead of 5 a week
rescue.requires: B2B sales and a local delivery route in one metro

rescue.change: Open the system: no pack lock, sell packs as convenience in one metro only
rescue.why: Fixes legal_platform_risk and the Keurig 2.0 graveyard pattern; cuts server dependency
rescue.requires: Accepting lower attach rate on packs

type_checks.note: Est. weekly box: ~$15 (33%) at 7 packs, ~$0 at 3 packs, since cold-chain shipping (~$11.50 a box, gel packs, dim-weight pricing) is fixed per box.
Est. 15% return rate x ~$245 per returned 30 lb press = ~$37 per unit (5% of price); opened packs are a total loss but cheap.
